  The Finance Sub- Committee recommended that the City Council should

7.  Fire  Study Options for Delivery  City Manager Russi reported on the Fire Study Options for Delivery of Fire
  of  Fire and EMS Services  and  EMS Services.  He  stated  that on August 25th, the City Council  held a
  study  session  regarding fire operations. The purpose  of the session  was to
  receive information on the initial proposal from Los Angeles County Fire
  District as well as an independent review of that proposal and existing fire
  operations.  Through that discussion, the Council requested further research be
  done as well as provide a 30- day public comment period before the matter was
  brought back to Council for further consideration.  Those elements  have now
  been completed and will be incorporated  into the original report.

  City Manager Russi asked Council for direction through one of the following
  actions:

  Option A-  Authorize the reimbursement agreement with the Los Angeles
  County Fire District,  and direct the City Manager and Interim Fire Chief to
  begin necessary meetings with County fire staff for negotiating terms for
  24, 000 to
  contracting EMS and Fire services to the County, and
  appropriate$

  fund that effort; or

  Option B - Direct staff to initiate steps outlined  in Messina' s report on
  improving various aspects of the current department operations including
  Standards of Coverage,  recruitment of a  Fire Chief, and expanded firefighters
  recruitment  efforts,  and  appropriate$  60, 000 to fund that effort.

  The City Council discussed the pros and cons of contracting for fire services or
  keeping Fire Department.  All were concerned for the safety of the community
  and fire staff.

  Mayor Pro Tem Carder stated she was against contracting with the County for
  fire services and she supported Option B.

  Mayor Hepburn,  and  Council Members Davis,  Crosby and Lau supported
  Option A, citing that the safety  of  the community was the most important.  In

  addition,  they directed the City Manager that when he meets with the County
  Fire District staff on terms for contracting for Fire and EMS services that he
  look into the City retaining ownership of the real property where Fire Station
  No. 3 is located.
